_comment: Prose templates for the chronicle renderer. Each event type maps to variants; the renderer picks deterministically per seed. Slots: {scribe} {house} {place} {day_ord} {season_ord} plus any event data keys. Voice rules: dry, literate, no exclamation marks, the road is patient and so is the prose. This file is where the book lives — add variants freely, the more the better.
season_began: In the {season_ord} season of {house}, {scribe} took up the pen.
The {season_ord} season fell to {scribe}, who had opinions about that.
It was the {season_ord} season, and the pen passed to {scribe}.
departed: {scribe} left {place} with {daylight} days of light in hand and less certainty than the ledger admits.
The caravan cleared the gate of {place} at first light, {daylight} days of it bought and paid for.
{scribe} walked out of {place} counting daylight like silver, {daylight} days of it.
arrived: The road gave {place} up without argument.
On the {day_ord} day, {place}, and nothing worse.
{place} passed beneath the caravan's feet and asked for nothing.
delayed: {place} took its toll in patience — {cost} days of light gone to waiting.
The road slowed at {place}, the way roads do when watched.
Two days were lost at {place}, and no one could afterwards say to what.
mishap: At {place}, the road collected: {lost}, and three days of light.
{place} was unkind. The caravan left lighter by {lost}.
Something went wrong at {place} in the ordinary way, and it cost {lost}.
peril_survived: {place} nearly kept {scribe}. It settled for four days of light.
There are prayers for what happened at {place}, and {scribe} used several.
{scribe} came through {place} alive, which the ledger records without comment.
shaken_down: A factor of House Urtenu examined the cargo at {place} with great courtesy and took {lost}.
The rival sail closed at {place}. The debt, as always, stood — paid this day in {lost}.
At {place}, papers were checked, opinions were held, and {lost} changed hands.
found_relic: In the silence of {place}, {scribe} found something the sea had not finished claiming.
{place} kept its dead and offered {scribe} a small thing in exchange for leaving.
Among the stones of {place}, an older road's leavings. {scribe} made a note.
entry_written: {scribe} stopped and wrote: a {entry_type} on {subject}. It cost {cost_days} of light, and it was the point.
Daylight went to ink at {place} — a {entry_type} concerning {subject}.
The pen came out at {place}. A {entry_type}: {subject}. The road will remember what {scribe} paid to know it.
turned_home: At {place} the road ran out of away. {scribe} turned for home.
{place}, copper-rich and jealous, marked the far end of the season. The caravan turned.
The outward road ended at {place}. Everything after this was returning.
returned: {scribe} came through the gate of {place} with {entries} entries in the ledger and the rest in aching feet.
Home. The ledger held {entries} entries, which is to say: the season had happened, and proof existed.
{place} received its scribe back. {entries} entries came home in the bags.
stranded: The light ran out at {place}, and the road kept {scribe}. What was not sent home was lost.
The season ended where it stood, at {place}. What {scribe} had not sent ahead never reached the archive.
{scribe} misjudged the arithmetic of daylight by very little, at {place}, which was enough.
fell: The road kept {scribe} at {place}. The House would learn of it from strangers.
{place} took {scribe}, as it had taken others, without malice and without appeal.
{scribe} fell at {place}. The unwritten died too — that is what unwritten means.
courier_sent: At {place}, {scribe} paid a runner and a seal to send {entries} entries home ahead of the news. Scribes do this when they have begun to doubt the return leg.
A copy of the ledger left {place} under seal — {entries} entries, travelling faster and safer than {scribe} now expected to.
{scribe} sent the ledger home from {place}: {entries} entries, a seal, and {media} sheets of the season's stock. The road was going badly, and this was the admission.
courier_delivered: A courier reached {place} carrying {entries} entries under the seal of {scribe}, who did not follow them home.
What remained of {scribe} arrived by hired hands: {entries} entries, folded into the archive of {house}.
The courier's satchel held {entries} entries. The archive of {house} took them in; the road kept the one who wrote them.
ledger_merged: The ledger merged into the archive of {house}: {entries} entries the House now cannot forget.
The archive grew by {entries} entries. Somewhere in the temple district, a scribe of the old school felt a chill.
{entries} entries, folded into the House's memory. The dead will thank {scribe} for this, eventually.
route_documented: With that, {route} was documented whole — three legs written down. A road anyone could walk. A road a caravan could walk alone.
The last leg went into the archive, and {route} became a written thing. What is written can be repeated.
{route}, complete in the archive. From this season forward, the road no longer required {scribe} — which was the entire idea.
caravan_returned: While the House slept, a caravan walked {route} on its own and came home with {income} shekels, weighed. The road remembered. It had been written down.
A caravan ran {route} unattended and returned {income} shekels to the House. No one living had to be anywhere.
{income} shekels arrived from {route}, earned by a road walking itself. The archive, as usual, said nothing and did everything.
succession: {scribe} inherited the House, the Archive, and the Concord's memory of {predecessor}.
The pen passed to {scribe}. What {predecessor} wrote remained; what {predecessor} knew did not.
{house} continued, as houses do, in the person of {scribe}, standing on everything {predecessor} left in writing.
